name: Ruzal Sitdikov
title: Synthetic chemist — electrocatalysis, sustainable catalysis & scale-up
summary: Ph.D. chemist with more than ten years of research in sustainable catalysis, electro-organic synthesis and reaction optimisation. I develop C–H functionalisation and late-stage functionalisation methods for complex molecules, map catalytic cycles to make reactions robust, and take lab-scale cascades towards scalable, greener processes. I also build small free software tools for teaching and learning chemistry.

apps.name: ChemEdit
apps.tagline: Structure editor & lab notebook for teaching
apps.text: A free educational tool for students and teachers: draw structures and double-click to edit them again, save them as ordinary files (SVG, Molfile, SDF, CDXML…), and practise keeping a lab notebook with stoichiometry, reaction schemes and a lab book. Works offline; nothing leaves your device.

apps.name: ChemGame
apps.text: Four short learning games for organic chemistry courses: link transformations, put synthetic routes in order, draw mystery molecules from clues, and play functional-group bingo. Free, offline, no sign-up.

competencies.items: Organic electrosynthesis & electrocatalysis (anodic/cathodic, paired), sustainable/green chemistry, photocatalysis, metal catalysis, cross-coupling (XEC, HAT), C–H activation, late-stage functionalisation, catalytic cascades, redox chemistry, isotope labelling (D, ¹³CD₃), click and supramolecular chemistry, mechanistic studies
Reaction scale-up to preparative scale, high-throughput screening and Bayesian optimisation, flow and electro reactors, process miniaturisation, data-driven optimisation workflows
NMR (1D/2D), MS (GC/LC-MS, ESI, HRMS, MALDI-TOF), GC, HPLC, UV-Vis, fluorescence, IR, cyclic voltammetry, potentiometry, synchrotron X-ray techniques, XRD, DLS, rheometry, thermal analysis
Glovebox and Schlenk techniques; microwave, photo-, electro-, flow and high-pressure reactors; crystal growth; chromatography systems; instrument maintenance and troubleshooting
ChemDraw, SciFinder/Reaxys, MestReNova/TopSpin, Mercury, Origin, LaTeX, Zotero/EndNote, automation; scientific illustration (Inkscape, Blender)
English (fluent), Swedish (professional working proficiency, B1/B2), Russian and Tatar (native)

points: Developing sustainable, atom-efficient catalytic cascades for complex small molecules.
Mapping catalytic cycles to make reactions more robust and predictable.
Synchrotron X-ray characterisation for structural and mechanistic insight.
Optimising reaction conditions for scale-up with integrated data-driven workflows.
Synthesised novel small-molecule hits within multidisciplinary drug-discovery teams.
Rapid validation of synthetic intermediates by LC-MS and NMR.
Translated biological targets into efficient synthetic routes.

experience.role: Research Scientist (O. Verho & A. Karlén groups)
points: Led the development of metalla-electrocatalytic C–H functionalisation for bioactive molecules and biomass valorisation.
Late-stage functionalisation directly on complex bioactive molecules; scale-up to preparative scale.
Sustainable C–H functionalisation protocols that minimise toxic metal use.
Set up and managed the electrochemistry laboratory; mentoring.
Designed and synthesised tunable redox-active mediators (ferrocene monolayers, Ru/Os complexes) for ion-to-electron transduction and sensing.
Trained 50+ students in GC-MS analytical chromatography.
Ni-catalysed electrochemical protocols for heterocycle synthesis and direct deuteration.
Electrochemical late-stage ¹³CD₃-methylation of drugs; isotope labelling supporting DMPK studies.
Maintained automated reactors and LC-MS; supervised interns.

experience.role: Postdoctoral Researcher (R. Leino group, Johan Gadolin scholar)
points: Enantioselective tin-mediated Barbier-type propargylation of unprotected carbohydrates.
“Clickable” mannitol-based supramolecular organogelators; nanoparticle modification and rheology.

experience.role: Postdoctoral Researcher (O. Ramström group, Visby scholar)
points: Multivalent glycodendrimer metal-cluster inhibitors against multiresistant E. coli.
Trehalose-based dendrons for carbon- and quantum-dot functionalisation.

experience.role: Visiting Researcher (W. Dehaen group, Erasmus Mundus)
points: New (thia)pillar[n]arene macrocycles for sensing and catalysis, structures proven by X-ray.
UV and NMR titrations of ligand binding; supervised a Master's project.

experience.role: Junior Researcher / Project Engineer (I. S. Antipin & I. I. Stoikov)
points: Multivalent (thia)calix[n]arenes and Si nanoparticles for biosensors and nanomaterials.
Supramolecular receptors for anions, cations and dicarboxylic acids; binding constants by UV-vis and fluorescence.
Laboratory safety, training and supervision of undergraduate projects; grant writing.
Galactose-modified multivalent calixarenes for the study of carbohydrate-binding proteins.
Regional award “Best PhD student in natural sciences in Tatarstan”; Rector's certificate of honour; RFBR research grant.
